Author: Narendra Kumar Vyas
Bench: Narendra Kumar Vyas
 
 High Court Of Chhattisgarh, Bilaspur
 Cra No. 996 of 2023
  Lomesh Rajput S/o Narendra Rajput Aged About 20 Years R/o Village
 Lamti, Police Station Patharia, District Mungeli (C.G.)
 ---- Appel
 Versus
  State of Chhattisgarh Through The Station House Officer, Police
 Station Patharia, District Mungeli (C.G.)
 ---- Responde

The appellant has filed this appeal under Section 14A of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (for short , "the Act, 1989") against the order dated 27-4-2023 passed by the learned Special Judge (Atrocities) Act, Mungeli, District Mungeli (CG) by which the regular bail of the appellant who has been arrested on 19-4-2023 in connection with Crime No 64 of 2023 for the offence punishable under Sections 509 (B), 376, 506, 34 of IPC and Section 67 and 67(A) of the Information Technology Act and Section 3 (i)(x) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 registered in Police Station Patharia,
District Mungeli (CG), has been rejected.

Further case of the prosecution is that the complainant has further stated that on 1-2-2023 one of the villagers has informed that obscene video has been communicated to her, therefore, it has been informed that prsent applicant has lodged complaint against Ishwar Verma.

Name of the appellant was not found in the case diary but on the memorandum statement of co-accused it has been brought on record that the same has been communicated by the present appellant, therefore, offence under Section 67 and 67(A) of the IT Act has been registered against the appellant.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant would submit that neither the appellant has neither prepared any obscene video of the prosecutrix nor committed any sexual intercourse with her.
The appellant was arrested on 19-4-2023 and more than three months have been lapsed.
He would further submit that the maximu sentence which can be awarded to the applicant is five years.
He would further submit that charge-sheet has already been filed and trial wil take considerable time folr its conclusion, therefore the appellant is entitled to be realsed on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State opposes the bail application.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the partiesand perused the record.

6. Considering submissions made by the appellant and further fact that no further interrogation is required and also considering the fact that the appellant is in jail since 19-4-2023 and trial will take consdierable time, I am inclined to release the appellant on bail.

7. Accordingly, the instant criminal appeal is allowed and the order dated 27-4-2023 (Annexure A/1)
passed by the court below is set aside.

The appellant is directed to be released on bail on his executing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.25,000/- with one local surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of the Trial Court for his appearance before the said Court as and when directed.
